title: Family Care & Flexible Leave Framework
author: Ava Patel
body:
## Overview

This document defines Redwood's Family Care & Flexible Leave Framework (the Framework). It consolidates statutory leave, company-paid caregiving leave, flexible part-time transitions, and short-term schedule accommodations into a single reference so employees and managers can make consistent, humane decisions. The intention is to support contributors through life events while keeping teams informed and minimizing operational disruption.

Key principles:
- Equity: similar personal circumstances should result in comparable support across roles and locations (subject to local law).
- Predictability: clear allowances, notice requirements, and payroll impacts.
- Flexibility: a spectrum of options from remote-first days to formal leaves and role-time reductions.
- Manager + People Ops partnership: managers approve operational feasibility; People Ops coordinates eligibility, pay, and compliance.

---

## Who this applies to

- All full-time and part-time employees of Redwood in North America and Europe.
- Specific statutory entitlements (e.g., EU parental leave variations, US state-level family leave) remain governed by local law; this Framework supplements statutory minimums where permitted.

---

## Family Care & Leave Types (summary table)

Leave Type | Company Allowance (paid) | Typical Notice | Manager action required | Notes
---|---:|---|---|---
Primary parental leave (birth/placement) | Up to 18 weeks full pay for primary caregiver* | 8 weeks recommended | Submit People Ops request; approve transition plan | *Top-up applied after statutory pay where applicable
Secondary parental leave | Up to 8 weeks full pay | 4 weeks recommended | People Ops notification | Can be taken in blocks 
Caregiving leave (serious family illness) | Up to 6 weeks at 100% pay, then unpaid up to 12 weeks | As soon as feasible | Manager + People Ops assessment | May require medical attestation depending on duration
Bereavement | 5 paid days for immediate family; manager discretion for extended absence | As soon as feasible | Manager notification | Extended support through EAP if needed
Flexible schedule (temporary) | N/A (adjusted FTE/pay) | 2 weeks notice recommended | Manager approval + People Ops payroll notice | Examples: 60% FTE for 3 months, compressed workweek
Emergency ad-hoc care days | 10 days/year (paid) | Day-of | Manager notification | For urgent short-term caregiving needs

Notes: this table is illustrative. Local statutory entitlements override company allowance where law requires higher benefits.

---

## Eligibility & How allowances interact with statutory pay

1. Always check local statutory rules first. People Ops maintains a per-region statutory matrix (see related_pages).
2. Company-paid allowances are provided as a top-up when statutory leave provides partial pay. Example: if statutory parental leave provides 6 weeks at 80% pay, Redwood will top to 100% for the first 6 weeks for eligible primary caregivers, subject to maximums above.
3. Eligibility window: generally employees with 6+ months tenure are eligible for the company top-up; exceptions can be approved on a case-by-case basis by People Ops for special circumstances.

---

## Process: Requesting leave or a flexible transition

1. Employee discusses preliminary plan with manager (informal).
2. Employee files a formal request via People Ops portal (HR-Portal -> Requests -> Leave). Provide expected dates, role transition plan (if applicable), and any supporting docs.
3. Manager completes the operational impact form outlining coverage (backfill, shift of responsibilities, product deadlines).
4. People Ops verifies eligibility, calculates pay/top-up, and issues a formal approval or a counter-proposal within 7 business days.
5. If approved, schedule a handover meeting and publish a team coverage plan.

Checklist for employees (submit with request):
- Proposed start/end dates (or flexible schedule parameters)
- Handover document link (see Templates section)
- Point-of-contact for coverage
- Preferred return-to-work arrangements (phased return? part-time?)

Manager checklist:
- Coverage plan and temporary ownership matrix
- Communication plan for stakeholders
- Proposed interim KPIs to track deliverables during transition

---

## Templates & examples

- Handover template (use internal docs template): includes active projects, dependences, expected blockers, emergency contacts.
- Phased return plan example: 50% FTE for first 4 weeks, 75% next 4 weeks, full thereafter; include explicit meeting cadence to reassess.
- Role transition example: temporary product owner assignment, 4-week shadowing period, reassign on-call duties.

CLI example for People Ops portal (internal tooling):
- hr-cli leave request --type caregiving --start 2026-05-01 --end 2026-06-12 --note "primary caregiver for parent surgery"
- hr-cli leave status --request-id 8765

---

## Compensation, benefits continuity, and performance reviews

- Payroll: company top-ups are processed on the normal payroll cycle; changes to FTE must be indicated 2 pay periods before the effective date to ensure accurate deductions.
- Benefits: health, retirement contributions, and stock vesting continue during paid leave. For unpaid leave > 30 days, contribution mechanics are described at People Ops -> Benefits Continuity.
- Performance reviews: time away is not a performance signal. Managers should avoid tying leave to calibration or compensation decisions. When review windows overlap with leave, managers should document performance data from the prior cycle and consult People Ops for fair handling.

---

## Manager guidance: balancing empathy and deliverability

1. Treat leave discussions confidentially and empathetically.
2. Focus on outcomes, not presenteeism: agree on deliverables the team can commit to while preserving the employee's recovery/care time.
3. Use the coverage template to identify minimal viable scope for the duration.
4. Escalate complex cases to People Ops (e.g., high-impact roles, extended leaves, or cross-border complications).

Manager escalation triggers:
- Expected absence longer than 12 weeks
- Unclear backfill path that threatens a major milestone
- Requests for role-level changes or promotions tied to leave periods

---

## Edge cases and cross-border considerations

- International hires: local statutory matrix maintained by People Ops. Some countries mandate longer parental benefits; the company will comply with local law and usually will not reduce by offering U.S.-style top-ups.
- Contractors: contractors are not eligible for company-paid leave but may request scheduling accommodations; invoke Manager/People Ops discretion.
- Role change during leave: coordinate with Talent & Compensation for effective dates and compensation proration rules.

---

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Can I take parental leave intermittently?
A: Intermittent leave is allowed for secondary caregivers in most regions; primary caregiver intermittent leave requires manager approval and a clear handover plan.

Q: Will taking leave affect my promotion timeline?
A: No. Promotions and calibration are based on documented performance outcomes. When relevant, managers should work with People Ops to adjust timelines fairly.

Q: Who covers urgent on-call responsibilities while I’m on leave?
A: Managers should identify a temporary on-call owner in the coverage plan. If the role lacks a clear backup, escalate to the hiring team for a short-term contractor.

---

## Ownership and maintenance

- Document owner: People Ops Benefits (Ava Patel).
- Review cadence: annual (every Q4) or after any major statutory change.
- Escalation contact: people-ops@redwood.com; for urgent manager support: on-call People Ops via Slack #people-ops.

---

## Appendix: quick reference (short bullets)

- Emergency ad-hoc care: 10 paid days/year; notify manager same day.
- Bereavement: 5 paid days for immediate family.
- Primary parental: up to 18 weeks company-paid top-up (see locality matrix).
- Secondary parental: up to 8 weeks company-paid.
- Eligibility: typically 6+ months tenure for company top-ups; exceptions possible.

For any questions not answered in this Framework, open a People Ops case via the HR portal or DM the People Ops lead.
